title: Sketchbot Designer Vinyl Toy
blurb: The retro-styled, pencil-wielding robot that started the studio. Self-produced from sketch to sculpt to 3D print to rotocast vinyl, Sketchbot launched in 2010 and spawned five colourway variants, resin exclusives and two sold-out DIY custom shows in NYC and LA.
body: Sketchbot began as a blog doodle in 2007 and became a 5.5" vinyl figure with a removable pencil accessory. The prototype was sculpted by hand, refined in Maya, rapid-prototyped, and cast in silicone before going to production.

Variant releases debuted at TOYSTREET NYC, San Diego Comic-Con and New York Comic-Con with My Plastic Heart, plus DesignerCon resin editions cast by Pretty In Plastic. In 2010 the platform hosted the Sketchbot Custom Show with dozens of guest artists.

title: Afternoon At The Museum
blurb: Proof of concept for the Epic Games MegaGrant: the Eye Pilots wander a brutalist museum of robots, rendered in real time in Unreal Engine.
body: A self-guided, non-linear museum in the World of Sketchbot. This UE4 proof of concept established the lighting, scale and character locomotion for the Museum of Untold Possibilities pitch.
Every gallery is a vignette: the Sketchbot history wing, Inktober, March of Robots and a gift-shop full of the studio's cast.

title: The Museum of Untold Possibilities
blurb: CoCo VR meets the World of Sketchbot. A MegaGrant pitch for a non-game VR museum with timed exhibitions, an AI robot docent and an Art Lab where visitors build and 3D-print their own robots.
body: I love being in VR. Most notably, the sense of awe and wonderment when allowed to roam freely, explore and interact. This piece falls into a non-game vertical, with emphasis on interaction, non-linear progression and DIY creation.

Phase One is the VR museum on Quest. Phase Two puts the Eye Pilots in their own puzzle game. Phase Three is a short-form series rendered in Unreal. The team: Steve Talkowski (creative director), Erik Anderson (Unreal engineer, Lumiere-winning TreeVR, Meow Wolf), Erik Desiderio (composer, Adventure Time VR, Star Trek Fleet Command).

title: Jammin' Alpacas
blurb: A stylised animated short: a band of alpacas, a space billboard and a lot of attitude. Full character pipeline from design through final render.
body: Designed, modeled, rigged, animated and lit in-house. The stills here are from the end-shot and reaction beats.

title: Autodesk Maya M4Y4
blurb: The official mascot for Autodesk Maya's Learning Channel. Designed, modeled and rendered to be real-time compliant so it lives inside the Maya viewport for training content.
body: I was brought on to design, model and render the new mascot for Autodesk Maya's Learning Channel. One of the key requirements was the character be real-time compliant for use in Maya's viewport for training purposes.

title: GIBCO Cells
blurb: Cell characters for GIBCO by Thermo Fisher Scientific: appealing, on-brand personalities for life-science media.
body: Concept exploration through to final rendered character line-up.

title: SCOOB! 3D Concept Art
blurb: 3D concept tests for the Mean Machine in Warner Animation Group's SCOOB!
body: Rapid 3D concept iterations exploring silhouette, surfacing and attitude for Dick Dastardly's Mean Machine.

title: Adobe VR Bot
blurb: A neon-lit robot for Adobe's VR storytelling push: a headset-wearing bot sculpting light in a smoky, tube-lit warehouse.
body: Modeled and rendered with a full look-dev pass; the neon environment was built to sell the 'painting in VR' idea.

title: Backrooms
blurb: Sketchbot lost in the liminal office. Built as a fully immersive USDZ environment for Apple Vision Pro Safari website environments.
body: An optimized 20 MB USDZ environment with baked lighting, assembled in Reality Composer Pro and served as a website environment.

title: BuddhaBot
blurb: The serene sacred robot at the end of the Eye Pilots' journey. Cover of 3D World issue 191.
body: From original sketch to a fully sculpted, rendered character, BuddhaBot became a recurring icon in the World of Sketchbot.

title: KeyShot 6 Avatar
blurb: The official avatar robot for the KeyShot 6 launch, with a four-page making-of tutorial in 3D World #198.
body: Designed for the gang at KeyShot to headline the KeyShot 6 launch. Variants explored colour, pose and material; a matcap-lighting workflow was written up for 3D World.

title: Beats by Dre
blurb: A cast of stylised characters for Beats by Dre: pirates, Elvis, gift-box Kingston and more.
body: Character design and modeling for a Beats campaign, delivered as posed, rendered line-ups.

title: Inktober 2012
blurb: Thirty-one days of ink robots.
body: A daily ink sketch for every day of October 2012.

title: Botober 2013
blurb: Inktober, but in 3D: a robot modeled and rendered every day.
body: Each day's bot went from block-out to render in a single sitting.

title: March of Robots 2014
blurb: The studio's first March of Robots, Dacosta Bayley's yearly robot-a-day challenge.
body: A month of daily robots, ending in a group shot of the whole squad.

title: March of Robots 2016
blurb: Twenty-seven robots in thirty-one days, from arcade cabinets to walking cameras.
body: Round three of March of Robots pushed material and lighting variety: painted metal, plastic toys, illustrated matte finishes.

title: RefBot
blurb: The referee robot made for the World Cup show at Crewest LA.
body: Built on the Sketchbot platform with a whistle, a card and a stern eye.

title: TikiBot
blurb: From a sketchbook page to a carved-wood tiki robot, with process screenshots along the way.
body: Sketch, ZBrush block-in, Maya retopology and a KeyShot wood-grain finish.

title: Browser Bots
blurb: Every web browser as a robot. Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Opera, Internet Explorer and Verold, plus the group shot.
body: A personal series turning browser logos into a squad of robots.

title: 3D Miscellany
blurb: Thirty-nine odds and ends: Meet Mat Sketchbot, HeartBot, OctoBot Beach Patrol, USBot, VoteBots, holiday cards, hex-mesh ZBrush studies and the VR Eye Pilot.
body: The overflow shelf of the studio: one-offs, holiday cards, contest entries and material tests.

title: Pumpkin Giant
blurb: A towering jack-o'-lantern robot, test-rendered in three colourways.
body: Design and look-dev for a seasonal giant.

title: Surge Protector
blurb: A Disney-style modeling test inspired by Bill Schwab's Wreck-It Ralph concept art.
body: Just finished up this model test using Maya, ZBrush 4R7 beta, and KeyShot. I was asked if I had anything in the Disney style in my modeling portfolio, and I hadn't. So I found some Wreck-It Ralph concept art from the amazing Bill Schwab to use as reference and inspiration.

title: TRON Immersive
blurb: An homage to the 1982 original, built as the studio's first spatial website environment for Apple Vision Pro. Step onto The Grid from Safari, with a Recognizer and a Tank rendered stereoscopically in the page.
body: The original TRON ignited my passion for computer animation when I first saw it at 16 in 1982. With the release of TRON: Ares, I decided to create an homage to the original as a proof-of-concept for my first spatial website environment for Apple Vision Pro.
Modeled and animated in Autodesk Maya. Textured in Adobe Substance Painter. Assembled in Reality Composer Pro. END OF LINE.
